claim: 1000ms held-key cliff exists in this benchmark
next_action: do not reopen without new metric
direct_observation: Dense held-key delay sweeps show the retained latency drop around the rich-text persistence interval.
allowed_inference: The benchmark has a real delay-dependent measurement boundary for held-key input.
blocked_inference: Generic user typing gets faster at 1000ms, or the cliff is only a plotting artifact.
next_evidence_if_claim_expands: Only needed if the claim expands from fixed-key benchmark behavior to product-wide typing behavior.

claim: Held key and complete keypress are different metrics
next_action: do not reopen without new metric
direct_observation: Matched tap/complete-keypress versus held-key rows do not share the same delay curve.
allowed_inference: A benchmark using Playwright held-key delay is not measuring the same workload as keypress-then-wait.
blocked_inference: Delay-between-characters, key hold, tap, and complete-keypress helper calls are interchangeable.
next_evidence_if_claim_expands: Repeat only when Playwright helper internals or CI helper spelling changes.

claim: Firefox similarity rules out Chrome-only EventDispatch wording
direct_observation: The controlled Firefox lane preserves a similar dip under comparable benchmark conditions.
allowed_inference: The dip should not be explained solely as Chrome's EventDispatch accounting.
blocked_inference: Firefox and Chromium necessarily share the same lower-level mechanism.
next_evidence_if_claim_expands: A same-grid, same-key-mode browser trace or sidecar artifact if browser-mechanism naming becomes the claim.

claim: Gutenberg persistence timing is an ordering marker, not a proven work-shift cause
direct_observation: Persistence markers and timer events align with the transition, while no-op/raw-action controls reject several simple store-work explanations.
allowed_inference: The Gutenberg state boundary is part of the event ordering that separates slow and fast retained-key classes.
blocked_inference: The timer callback makes the next key faster by doing work that otherwise would have been charged to that key.
next_evidence_if_claim_expands: Per-retained-key task/runtime joins that show the callback, subsequent key event, and browser/runtime checkpoint state without perturbing ordering.

claim: Ordinary post-keyup waiting is not sufficient
next_action: do not reopen without new metric
direct_observation: Raw CDP ordinary waits from very short delays through multi-second delays do not reproduce the same fast class.
allowed_inference: Sleeping longer, draining queued JS, or letting the page rest is not enough by itself.
blocked_inference: Any delay past the timer should automatically produce the low-latency class.
next_evidence_if_claim_expands: No more ordinary-wait extensions unless browser revision or helper family changes.

claim: CPU/QoS may modulate absolute latency but is not named
direct_observation: External CPU and finite-duration controls move absolute latency while preserving several benchmark orderings.
allowed_inference: System state is a plausible contributor to residual absolute time and portability.
blocked_inference: Frequency, QoS, cache, or scheduler policy has been identified as the cause.
next_evidence_if_claim_expands: Sidecar-accepted runs with joined frequency, residency, QoS, runnable-latency, and power windows.

claim: Startup-wait reduction must be gated by non-q50 readiness
direct_observation: Startup-wait artifacts show retained aggregates and early-key distributions, but readiness/failure/resource fields decide whether wait can be removed.
allowed_inference: A shorter wait can be considered only when q50 and readiness fields move together.
blocked_inference: A lower retained q50 alone means CI can safely remove startup wait.
next_evidence_if_claim_expands: Real Performance Tests artifact retaining failures, retries, resources, first-key tails, run order, and environment metadata.

claim: Pattern wait can probably be shortened locally, but rollout is not closed

allowed_inference: The current fixed wait is locally conservative and not always needed.
blocked_inference: The local result is enough to change CI across mac, container, and Site Editor paths.
next_evidence_if_claim_expands: CI/mac/container validation with predicate, resource quiet, preview/canvas, actionability, failures, and retained rows.
